### Series 2

- Fair image quality

### Series 3

|---|---|---|
| Perihilar/marking prominence | Improving | Progressive decrease in severity/confidence from Series 1 (moderate, left-predominant) → Series 2 (mild, right-predominant) → Series 3 (subtle, bilateral, low confidence) |

| Costophrenic angles/pleura | Stable | Preserved in all three sessions, no effusion |

## Overall Impression
Across the three chronologically ordered single-view radiographs, there is a general trend toward **improvement or resolution** of mild, nonspecific perihilar/bibasilar opacities/markings. The laterality of the finding shifted between sessions (left-predominant → right-predominant → bilateral/subtle), which is more consistent with technical variability (rotation, exposure, positioning) than a true evolving focal pathology. Cardiac size, mediastinal contour, and pleural spaces remained stable and unremarkable throughout. No consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax developed at any point.

If the observed trend continues, the mild perihilar/bibasilar changes are expected to further resolve or remain low-grade, consistent with a self-limited or artifactual process. - Repeat radiography with improved technique (adequate exposure, patient positioning) and consider a lateral view
- Correlate with clinical symptoms (dyspnea, cough, fever, orthopnea) and vital signs
